title: Drain the Shallows
coreMove: Quantify shallow obligations, cap them deliberately, and redesign communication so depth has room to happen.
sourcePressure: The source frame says to reduce shallow obligations, constrain email sprawl, and defend time for deep work.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version tells people to ignore email; the chapter must show deliberate constraints that preserve necessary coordination while shrinking shallow spread.

exampleSpecs.domain: a city permitting office redesigning applicant questions
exampleSpecs.audience: a public manager whose staff loses depth to repetitive clarification loops
exampleSpecs.stakes: permit reviews slow down when every applicant email becomes custom consulting
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she replaces open-ended email replies with a checklist and two weekly review windows, then tracks the hours returned to technical review
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a permit inbox sorted beside a marked-up application checklist

exampleSpecs.domain: a biotech lab manager protecting experiment-design time
exampleSpecs.audience: a lab manager whose coordination work keeps expanding
exampleSpecs.stakes: poorly designed assays waste expensive samples
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he calculates how many hours reagent questions consumed, then creates a request form that prevents same-day scattered pings
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a freezer inventory screen beside a notebook page labeled assay design

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional airline maintenance planner batching routine approvals
exampleSpecs.audience: a planner whose deep sequencing work is broken by small approvals
exampleSpecs.stakes: aircraft sit idle if maintenance slots are sequenced badly
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after a delayed aircraft, she counts approval interruptions and moves routine signoffs into two fixed batches
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a maintenance bay schedule with one aircraft tail number highlighted

exampleSpecs.domain: a university admissions office reducing essay-review interruptions
exampleSpecs.audience: a reviewer whose judgment requires sustained comparison
exampleSpecs.stakes: strong applicants blur together when review is fragmented
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she logs shallow interruptions during one review block, then sets a question-routing rule before the next batch
exampleSpecs.firstImage: three application essays open beside an interruption tally sheet

exampleSpecs.domain: a civil engineering firm constraining client revision requests
exampleSpecs.audience: a project lead whose team keeps reworking drawings from scattered comments
exampleSpecs.stakes: stormwater calculations drift when revisions arrive one at a time
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she tells the client all comments must arrive in one marked drawing packet by Thursday, then protects Friday for calculation updates
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a stormwater drawing covered with mismatched comment bubbles

exampleSpecs.domain: a culinary test kitchen limiting supplier questions
exampleSpecs.audience: a recipe developer whose shallow coordination displaces recipe trials
exampleSpecs.stakes: a national rollout recipe stays unstable without uninterrupted test batches
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she groups supplier questions into a single midday call and uses the reclaimed morning for three controlled sauce trials
exampleSpecs.firstImage: three labeled sauce cups beside a supplier question sheet

skillTargets: quantify shallow work before reducing it
design constraints for email and coordination
distinguish necessary shallow work from sprawl
evaluate whether a communication rule defends depth without blocking essential work

tryThisNowSpec: Find one recurring shallow exchange and write a single constraint that would batch it, clarify it, or make it unnecessary.
